proposals.evidence: DEDR1391 explicitly gives Tamil kaṟi raw or boiled meat/vegetables and Malayalam kaṟi meats/vegetables/hot condiments. These southern survey kari meat responses select the meat sense of that culinary family, retaining the source non-retroflex rhotic spelling. Precise inter-lect transmission is not established by the widespread culinary term alone. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1254 gives Tamil kayiṟu, Malayalam kayaṟu rope/cord and Kodagu kērï. Selected survey kayir-/kavar-/kagar-/kahar- forms are proposed comparative lect reflexes of the same rope stem, preserving intervocalic glide, labial, velar or fricative notation. More divergent Muthuvan kadɨrɨ/kadarɨ responses are excluded pending stronger sound evidence. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5276 gives Tamil valatu right side, Malayalam valam right side, Kannada bala, Kodagu balate, Telugu vala and Parji vela key right hand. These simple survey vala-/bala- forms preserve the strong/right family and source adjectival endings. Parji velā is the right-side stem without hand; correctness-sense sariyāna responses and longer compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

Selected southern survey vayar-/vagar-/bagar- and contracted vēr-/vār-/bēr- forms preserve this belly family; minority-lect assignments are comparative extensions retaining source vowels and consonants, not separate claimed dictionary attestations.
